landing.metaDescription: A network of exchange and solidarity for Egyptian cultural organizations.
landing.heroTag: When good goes around, it grows
landing.heroLede: A network of exchange and solidarity for Egyptian cultural organizations. What one organization has in surplus can meet another's need, using the Shahamham network currency instead of draining cash or waiting for donors.

about.title: A neighborly economy
about.lede: Egyptian cultural organizations work under the pressure of donor economics: short-term funding, competition for scraps, and idle assets in every office. Shahamham revives an old Egyptian logic — the gam'eya that circulates money among neighbors and the pantry that preserves good for the household.

features.title: Mutual credit
features.body: Each organization offers what it has and receives what it needs; accounts are recorded in the network currency rather than cash.

features.title: Surplus becomes value
features.body: An empty venue, an idle camera, or an extra hour from a designer all become value instead of going unused.

features.title: Democratic governance
features.body: Major decisions are made by member organizations through voting, not by a central administration.

how.title: Four steps, a cycle that completes

steps.title: Join
steps.body: Join by invitation from a member organization or the Shahamham team.

steps.title: Offer
steps.body: Publish your services and resources on Namliya in the network currency.

steps.title: Exchange
steps.body: Request, agree in writing, and deliver your work.

steps.title: Review
steps.body: A shared reputation grows through every completed exchange.

faq.title: Before you join
faq.lede: Click on a question to open the answer — so the page stays simple on the eye.

items.question: Is Shahamham money?
items.answer: No. Shahamham is a unit of account inside the network that records what you offered and received; it cannot be spent outside the network or converted to cash.

items.question: Who can join?
items.answer: Active Egyptian cultural organizations may join by invitation from a member organization or nomination by the Shahamham team.

items.question: What if my balance becomes negative?
items.answer: That is part of mutual credit. A credit limit and support help restore balance, without interest or penalties.

items.question: What prevents misuse?
items.answer: Monthly service limits, visible satisfaction signals, mediation, and member voting for major decisions.

contact.title: Talk to us
contact.lede: The network is still in its first year, and every note helps guide what comes next. If your organization sees itself here, or you have a question, we are listening.
